name: Leadership & Management
purpose: Individually authored episode questions and coverage boundaries for Leadership & Management. The subject progression is organized by concrete content rather than a topic-by-angle multiplication.

topics.question: What distinguishes formal authority from influence in a working team?
topics.coverage: Compare decision rights, expertise, trust and accountability through consented or fictional cases; avoid treating a job title as proof of leadership quality.

topics.question: How can a leader's stated values be compared with actual decisions?
topics.coverage: Trace resource allocation, incentives and documented tradeoffs; distinguish a public slogan from observed practice without guessing private motives.

topics.question: Why can a team's success be difficult to attribute to its leader alone?
topics.coverage: Compare selection, resources, inherited conditions and contributors; avoid a single-hero account built from retrospective praise.

topics.question: How can a manager delegate an outcome without hiding critical constraints?
topics.coverage: Use a fictional assignment with authority, dependencies, resources and review points; distinguish delegation from transferring blame without control.

topics.question: What makes a team goal measurable without letting the metric replace the purpose?
topics.coverage: Compare objective, indicator, unintended incentives and quality checks in an original project; avoid treating a target's achievement as complete success.

topics.question: Why can unclear decision ownership create repeated meetings?
topics.coverage: Map proposal, consultation, approval and escalation in a bounded workflow; distinguish a useful responsibility model from a universal reorganization recipe.

topics.question: How can coordination change when tasks depend tightly on one another?
topics.coverage: Compare handoffs, feedback speed, shared information and failure recovery; avoid assuming every team needs the same level of process.

topics.question: What distinguishes coaching a skill from evaluating a person's performance?
topics.coverage: Compare purpose, evidence, authority and next steps through fictional conversations; avoid turning workplace support into therapy or diagnosis.

topics.question: How can a manager make feedback fair when only some work is highly visible?
topics.coverage: Inspect task records, access, contribution and opportunity with consented examples; do not equate office presence with performance.

topics.question: Why can a development plan fail despite well-written goals?
topics.coverage: Compare practice opportunities, feedback, time, resources and follow-up; avoid attributing every shortfall to employee motivation.

topics.question: How can peer learning be designed without forcing one expert to do unpaid invisible teaching?
topics.coverage: Map workload, recognition, access and bounded responsibilities; distinguish voluntary sharing from an unlimited support obligation.

topics.question: What does psychological-safety research measure in actual teams?
topics.coverage: Inspect original scales, study designs, outcomes and context; distinguish speaking-up climate from absence of disagreement or accountability.

topics.question: How can disagreement about a task become a personal conflict?
topics.coverage: Compare observable communication, roles and resource pressures in a fictional case; avoid diagnosing personalities or inferring malicious intent.

topics.question: What should a leader investigate when team members stop raising problems?
topics.coverage: Examine response history, incentives, access and consented accounts; distinguish possible causes from conclusions based on silence alone.

topics.question: How can a team repair a failed handoff without beginning with a search for a culprit?
topics.coverage: Reconstruct expectations, information, timing and system conditions; preserve individual accountability where supported rather than assuming either system or person explains everything.

topics.question: How can a decision record distinguish a reasonable process from a fortunate outcome?
topics.coverage: Document available evidence, alternatives, assumptions and review triggers in an original scenario; avoid hindsight-based scoring.

topics.question: What does a premortem add to ordinary project planning?
topics.coverage: Compare identified failure paths, evidence and mitigations using published methods; distinguish generated risks from predictions that they will occur.

topics.question: When should a team escalate a decision rather than continue collecting information?
topics.coverage: Map stakes, reversibility, authority and deadline in a fictional case; avoid prescribing a personal legal, safety or financial decision.

topics.question: How can a retrospective lead to a testable change rather than a list of complaints?
topics.coverage: Connect one observed failure, a bounded intervention, an owner and review evidence; avoid assuming every event has a single root cause.

topics.question: How can leadership opportunities be evaluated for unequal access rather than only unequal outcomes?
topics.coverage: Inspect assignment criteria, sponsorship, workload and official records with privacy protections; avoid inferring discrimination in a real case without evidence.

topics.question: What should a leader clarify when a conflict of interest may affect a decision?
topics.coverage: Use current organizational policies and applicable official rules; distinguish disclosure, recusal and independent review without providing individual legal advice.

topics.question: Why can requesting candor be insufficient when the listener controls promotion or pay?
topics.coverage: Examine power, anonymity limits, retaliation protections and consented experiences; do not promise a survey guarantees safety.

topics.question: How can ethical leadership be assessed when commercial targets conflict with service obligations?
topics.coverage: Trace documented duties, choices, affected groups and oversight; avoid reducing a real dispute to an inspirational quotation.

categories.title: Change, distributed work and leadership narratives

topics.question: What does a change plan need beyond announcing the new structure?
topics.coverage: Compare work design, training, transition resources, feedback and affected staff accounts; distinguish rollout activity from adoption and useful outcomes.

topics.question: How can leadership in remote teams avoid making constant visibility a proxy for contribution?
topics.coverage: Map explicit outputs, access, communication windows and support using consented accounts; avoid surveillance-based scoring or assuming every role can be asynchronous.

topics.question: Why can a crisis alter the balance between consultation and rapid decisions?
topics.coverage: Use a documented public organizational case with authority, timelines and evidence; distinguish retrospective speculation from available choices at the time.

topics.question: How can succession planning include knowledge transfer rather than only naming a replacement?
topics.coverage: Trace responsibilities, relationships, documentation and access in an invented team; avoid exposing confidential personnel plans.

topics.question: How can a leadership-training programme be evaluated beyond participant satisfaction?
topics.coverage: Compare behavior, team outcomes, selection, controls and follow-up in original evaluations; avoid attributing all later performance to the course.

topics.question: What is missing when a leadership lesson is drawn only from successful executives?
topics.coverage: Inspect survivorship, context, inherited advantages and contradictory cases; distinguish a useful anecdote from a tested rule.

topics.question: How can a biography-based episode credit followers and institutions alongside the leader?
topics.coverage: Use primary records, multiple perspectives and specific decisions; avoid inventing private dialogue or treating influence as proof of moral virtue.

synthesis.requirements: Define the rival claims and their evidence standards. Compare sources on equal terms, separate empirical findings from values or interpretations and do not imply that all positions have equal evidential support.
source_leads: the original sources behind the compared claims
explicit definitions and measurement methods
independent critiques with traceable evidence

community.requirements: Use consented participant accounts, local records and the community's own descriptions. Include differences of position, access and power; testimony is not a representative survey or clinical proof.
source_leads: consented interviews and oral histories
community publications and local records
field notes with method and consent documented

civic.requirements: Use the current official legal text, policy, procedure or public dataset for a specific jurisdiction and date. Distinguish written rules, implementation and lived access; give no personal legal or financial conclusion.
source_leads: official laws, rules and administrative guidance
audits, judgments and public service records
consented accounts from affected people and qualified specialists

technical.requirements: Use the actual system documentation, a worked implementation and measurements. Identify inputs, outputs, constraints, tolerances, failure conditions and the limits of the example. Do not provide hazardous construction or unauthorized access procedures.
source_leads: original engineering papers
official versioned product or standards documentation
test reports and drawings with clear provenance

science.requirements: Use original observations or experiments, an appropriate scientific reference and the actual measurement method. Distinguish mechanisms, correlations, model assumptions, uncertainty and limits of generalization.
source_leads: original research reports and data
research-institution observation records
methods papers and current scientific reference works
